newsitem.title: CANADA: Poll shows Canada Liberals in gradual downtrend.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows Canada Liberals in gradual downtrend.

text.p: Canada's ruling Liberals continue to slip gradually but still stand a good chance of gaining another majority in elections expected this year, according to a poll released on Thursday.

The poll showed the Liberals have not recovered from the fallout of their failure to scrap a general sales tax, a disastrous performance in December by Prime Minister Jean Chretien at a televised town hall meeting with Canadians, and the government's handling of its involvement in Somalia.
The Liberals won support from 45 percent of those polled. The closest rival party gained only 19 percent support.

"This continues a gradual downward trend in the Liberals' support (from 57 percent last July, 52 percent last October, 47 percent in November and 46 percent in December), but it still places the Liberals above their 1993 election showing and solidly within majority government range," the poll said.
It was taken by Angus Reid on behalf of the Southam News chain, covering 1,519 Canadian voters from January 21-27. The poll had a margin of error of 2.5 percentage points 19 times out of 20.
The Conservative Party recovered to 19 percent from 16 percent in the 1993 election. They polled at 16 percent support in December.
The Reform Party languished at 11 percent, down from their 19 percent 1993 election showing and 14 percent in December.
The separatist Bloc Quebecois polled 11 percent and the leftist New Democratic Party stood at 10 percent.
Elections must be held by October 1998 but are widely expected to be held this spring or fall.
